correctness.rationale: For every complex quadratic, λp(ζ)+conjugate(λ)p(conjugate ζ)=a0+a1 by three exact coefficient identities, yielding the sharp universal 2/sqrt3 upper bound. The explicit polynomial has norm exactly one from the identity |2+4e^{it}−e^{2it}|²=27−8(cos t−1/2)². Equality forces two fixed point values and hence a one-parameter difference c(z²−z+1); two independent boundary stationarity equations force c=0. Exact independent re-derivation of boundary steps and packaged SymPy algebra checker reproduced every critical computation. This is an analytic proof over all complex quadratics, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: Successful published-finding corpus claim, alias and exact-parameter queries found no matching coefficient functional; existing matched quadratic results use different norms and objects. The directly relevant 2026 paper explicitly labels M_{1,3} <= 1/2+1/sqrt(2) as an upper bound, strictly weaker than the proved exact norm 2/sqrt3; its special exact theorems have incompatible coefficient patterns. Strongest historical risks, Shapiro (1952) and Rogosinski (1962), are specifically disclosed and do not supply observed dominating coverage.
residual_risks: Rogosinski, Mathematica Scandinavica 10 (1962), 53–70, has a plausible general linear-functional title; publisher PDF fetch failed and an authorized alternate retrieval returned no extractable text, so its full mathematical contents were not assessed.

H. S. Shapiro 1952 MIT PhD thesis is cited for an abstract node theorem and particular examples, but the original thesis full text was not obtained; priority risk remains for an unindexed example or appendix.

Other pre-database classical extremal-polynomial sources or equivalent dual interpolation certificates may record the precise constant; novelty is a best-evidence judgment, not a global uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The parameter (n,d)=(1,3) is the smallest nontrivial odd d not handled by Newman in the canonical 1952 Shapiro coefficient-partial-sum problem; the 2026 primary paper singles it out as an example of a nonsharp newly obtained bound. Exact resolution is an intrinsically motivated natural norm/invariant, not an arbitrary parameter substitution: the new sharp constant, explicit optimal nodes and complete extremizer rigidity improve a live displayed benchmark. This closes a sharply defined initial case without implying or claiming the general problem.
